bars.L1a: 1 m level, upright, >=8 strict alternating touchdowns, terminal stable hold (5 s). Never observed passing.
bars.L1b: L1a + Stable Walker contract: df>=1.00 m/120 s, efficiency>=0.70, maxCrossTrack<=0.15 m, |dl|<=0.15 m, reverse<=0.10 m, tilt<=0.45 rad after 5 s, no fall/damage/non-finite/saturation/forbidden non-pad support. THE OPEN PROBLEM.
bars.L1c: L1b + tracking over W=max(30 s,10L/v): velocity MAE<=max(0.005 m/s,0.15v), step MAE<=max(0.015 m,0.20L).
bars.L1d: Robustness under declared variation with held-out qualification cases. The completion condition.
bars.L2: Two runs of the same inputs under TWO DIFFERENT recorded renamings produce an identical deterministicProjection(frame) after remapping references. Distinct from D1: D1 fixes the renaming seed and varies nothing, so it cannot catch identity dependence.
bars.D1: Same blueprint, input trace AND renaming seed => identical deterministicProjection(frame) hash, two processes, both clocks. The projection excludes wall-clock timings, identifier mappings and diagnostic metadata.
bars.P1: Named scene on a named machine holds >=30 fps interactively. Measure before setting.
bars.S1: A hostile controller cannot escape, hang, or read undeclared state.
bars.F1: A target player, unassisted and untutored, builds something that moves within 15 minutes of first launch, and wants to build a second thing. Judged by watching a person.
bars.F2: Build-loop latency: place -> connect -> run under 2 s, with no compile step the player can perceive.
bars.F3: A player who did not build the machine can say why it failed from the post-mortem alone.
bars.F4: Ten minutes of unassisted play yields one moment of visible delight and no moment of 'I don't know what this wants from me'.
